test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the difference between displacement and distance?

options.text: Distance includes direction; displacement does not
Displacement includes direction; distance does not

solution:
The correct answer is __**Displacement includes direction; distance does not**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
__ 

• **Displacement** is a vector quantity that specifies the shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final positions of an object, along with the direction of movement. 

• **Distance**, on the other hand, is a scalar quantity that measures the total length of the path traveled by an object, irrespective of the direction. 

• Displacement can have a positive, negative, or zero value depending on the direction of motion, while distance is always positive and cannot be negative. 

• For example, if an object moves 10 meters forward and then 10 meters backward to its starting point, the displacement is 0 meters (due to no net change in position), while the distance is 20 meters. 

• Displacement considers direction and magnitude, making it more specific for indicating the change in position, whereas distance only measures magnitude, making it less specific. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Vector Quantity:** 

• A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. Examples include displacement, velocity, acceleration, and force. 

• Displacement is a vector quantity because it specifies both the magnitude (shortest distance) and direction. 
 
 

• **Scalar Quantity:** 

• A scalar quantity has only magnitude and no direction. Examples include distance, speed, mass, and temperature. 

• Distance is a scalar quantity because it measures only the magnitude of the path traveled. 
 
 

• **Applications:** 

• Displacement is used in physics for calculations involving motion, such as determining velocity and acceleration. 

• Distance is commonly used for practical purposes like measuring travel lengths or determining road routes. 
 
 

• **Example:** 

• If a person walks 3 km north and then 4 km east, the distance traveled is 7 km, while the displacement (using Pythagoras theorem) is 5 km northeast. 

• This highlights the difference between the total path traveled (distance) and the shortest path between two points (displacement). 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Directional Significance:** Displacement’s inclusion of direction makes it crucial for vector-based calculations in physics, while distance is used for scalar measurements. 

• **Zero Displacement:** If an object returns to its starting point after movement, displacement is zero, but distance measures the total path traveled. 

• **Real-Life Scenarios:** Distance is practical for everyday usage (e.g., driving or running), while displacement is essential for scientific experiments and modeling motion. 

• **Geographical Representation:** In maps, displacement is represented as straight-line distance between two points, while distance considers the curved or actual traveled path.
